title: Exterior Painting in Micanopy, FL | Under the Oak Canopy
description: Exterior painting in Micanopy, FL for homes under heavy oak shade: mildew treatment, rot repair, flexible caulk, and 100% acrylic. Up to 10-year warranty.
heroIntro: Shade from Micanopy's live oaks keeps walls damp, feeds mildew, and slows drying after every storm. Our exterior system is built to handle moisture first and color second.

questions: Why does paint fail faster on shaded parts of my house?
How do you handle mildew before painting an exterior?
When is the best season to paint outside in Micanopy?

sections.h2: Shade is the main challenge here
body: Most exterior advice in Florida is about sun. In Micanopy, the bigger issue is often the opposite. Under a heavy oak canopy, walls and trim can stay damp for days after rain, and the north and east faces may barely see direct light. That constant moisture feeds mildew and algae, softens wood at the bottom of siding and around windows, and makes old paint lift from underneath.

Add humidity above 75% for months each summer, afternoon storms several days a week from June into September, and leaf litter that clogs gutters and spills water down fascia, and you get a house that needs exterior painting built around moisture control.

sections.h2: Our exterior system for shaded homes
bullets: Soft wash and treat mildew at the root, not just on the surface
Inspect fascia and soffits wherever gutters overflow, and repair water damage
Take moisture readings on suspect wood and wait for it to dry before coating
Replace rotted siding, sills, trim, and fascia rather than painting over them
Scrape to a sound edge, sand gloss, and re-caulk joints with flexible sealant
Spot-prime bare wood, then two full coats of 100% acrylic on siding and trim
body: Sprayed surfaces are back-brushed or back-rolled where penetration matters, which is especially important on rough or weathered wood.

Not every wall is shaded. Where a gap in the canopy lets the afternoon sun hit a south or west wall, that side chalks and fades faster than the rest of the house. We note each elevation's exposure during the walkthrough and adjust prep and product where needed. Windows deserve special attention, too; our article on cracked paint on window frames explains why.

October through May is the best window for exterior work. In summer we start early and watch dew point and radar, and under heavy shade we allow extra dry time before coating. A full exterior typically runs three to seven working days plus wash and dry time; older homes with more repair take longer.

Every Micanopy exterior carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, on top of the manufacturer's product warranty. If you have a shaded porch or deck too, see deck staining in Micanopy. For whole-house planning, visit residential painting in Micanopy, and read our guide to mold on siding for background.

faqs.q: Why is my north wall peeling and green while the rest looks fine?
faqs.a: Shade keeps that wall damp, which lets mildew grow and moisture work under the paint. It needs a mildew treatment, a moisture check, and any soft wood replaced before repainting.

faqs.q: Can you paint while the oaks are dropping leaves and pollen?
faqs.a: Yes. We wash immediately before painting, protect fresh surfaces where we can, and plan around the heaviest drop periods when possible.

faqs.q: What paint do you use on old wood siding?
faqs.a: 100% acrylic from Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore, over spot-primed bare wood. Penetrating stain is an option where you want the wood grain to show.
